name: Surgical Wound Healing, Collagen Dynamics and Abnormal Scarring

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Schwartz's Principles of Surgery
clinicalPearls: Four phases of wound healing: Hemostasis (platelets, fibrin), Inflammation (neutrophils then macrophages), Proliferation (fibroblasts, granulation tissue), Remodeling
Proliferation phase features type III collagen; remodeling replaces it with organized type I collagen bundles cross-linked by lysyl oxidase
Wound tensile strength reaches 20% at 3 weeks and plateaus at maximum 80% of uninjured skin at 1 year
Hypertrophic scars remain confined within original incision margins; keloids invade normal surrounding tissue and have high recurrence
Abdominal wound dehiscence typically presents on postoperative days 5-8 with sudden serosanguinous pink discharge soaking dressings
reference.pathophysiology: Abnormal wound healing reflects dysregulated cytokine signaling. Excessive TGF-beta and PDGF signaling alongside impaired apoptosis of myofibroblasts produces keloids and hypertrophic scars. Scurvy (Vitamin C deficiency) impairs prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase, preventing collagen triple-helix stabilization and causing wound breakdown.
additionalInvestigations: Clinical inspection and physical examination of wound margins
Histopathological biopsy with Masson trichrome staining in atypical scarred lesions
High-frequency ultrasound of surgical scar for deep seroma or fascial gap
